top_signal.title: Bakery Owner | Drowning in work and things always slip through the cracks. How do you do this?
top_signal.summary: A little bit of context, I own three brick and mortar cake shops. 2026 has been a brutal year to be honest. Still profitable, can't complain, but sales are steeply down.    But, my question is about Ops. There is always so many things happening, fires coming in, etc. Now, I know, business of my size needs SOPs and checklists, etc., and we do, but I am not talking about managing the work of employees, but managing my own work. Things like "review ads", "come up with the next batch of ads", "brief the content creator", "update google profile", "approve payroll", "do the books", "plan/strategize location A sales growth", "analyze customer complaints", and so much more. There is just so many of those. I am not involved in day to day baking related activities and mostly do admin/ops stuff like this, mostly remote/from home, but the processes/tools I currently use don't seem to cut it as I always find myself behind certain things. Nothing crazy individually taken, but combined they compound. Like right now I am behind in ads review, and books, and updating employee training materials.   How's everyone managing their ops tasks? Just looking for a clean, organized way/structure of staying on top of everything.       submitted by     /u/Remarkable_Breath_42       [link]       [comments]
